subject: Proposal: Dedicated Burst Add-on Structure & Cooldown SLAs
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <acme-procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Dedicated Burst Add-on Structure & Cooldown SLAs

Hi Jorge / procurement team,

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Attached is a concise proposal for the Dedicated burst add-on we discussed (RDW-burst-pricing-v3.pdf). Key points up front:

- Burst add-on tiers: Pay-as-you-burst (on-demand), Burst Pack A (monthly top-up, lower unit rate), Burst Pack B (committed burst capacity, lowest unit rate).
- Surge rate (per-token premium) scales down with higher commit and is capped per-burst.
- Cooldown policy: a short cooldown after sustained bursts to ensure cluster stability; details and alternatives included in the attachment.
- Throughput guarantees: baseline throughput per reserved GPU pool; bursts are best-effort but we offer a throughput SLO backstop for Burst Pack B within regional capacity constraints.

Questions for you:
1) What monthly surge budget cap would procurement prefer to hard-cap (to avoid large unplanned invoices)?
2) Do you need burst consumption to count toward the reserved commit for true-up accounting, or kept separate as edge usage?

Request: please review and share the procurement team's risk/limit preferences. If this looks directionally right I can send a short SOW and updated Term Sheet for signature.

Attachments: RDW-burst-pricing-v3.pdf

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182
From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@acme.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <acme-procurement@acme.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Dedicated Burst Add-on Structure & Cooldown SLAs

Monica — thanks for the overview and the PDF. A couple of clarifying items from procurement's side:

- Cooldown windows: can you confirm how the cooldown is measured? Is it per-GPU pool (global to our account) or per-requester/route? We run several high-throughput routes and want to avoid a single long job blocking bursts for other teams.
- Billing treatment: does burst consumption draw down the reserved commit (i.e., reduce the remaining committed tokens) or is it always billed as a separate add-on?
- Surge cap: procurement prefers to cap uncommitted spend. We are thinking of a $25k monthly cap on surge beyond the commit. Is there a way to automatically throttle or failover when the cap is reached?

Also, can you share an example invoice for a month with a 1M-token commit + 300k burst usage under the proposed pack pricing so we can model our budget?

Thanks — Jorge
Jorge Ramos
Director, AI Platforms
Acme Corp
jorge.ramos@acme.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: Dedicated Burst Add-on Structure & Cooldown SLAs

Monica / Marcus — internal notes and suggested concessions before we respond to Acme: 

- Cooldown approach (proposed): implement two-tier cooldowns:
  * Short bursts (<5 minutes of sustained elevated throughput): no enforced cooldown (to support quick spikes).
  * Extended bursts (>5 minutes sustained or >100k tokens in a 15-min window): trigger a 30-minute account-level cooldown on additional burst top-ups to protect cluster stability.
- Billing treatment: offer option A (default): burst billed as separate add-on, does not draw down commit. Option B (for Pack B customers): allow burst to draw down commit at a discounted internal transfer rate if they elect a 12-month increased commit (adds complexity but appeals to finance teams).
- Surge cap handling: we can implement a soft-throttle + notification at 80% of the cap and a hard throttle when the $ cap is hit; need written acceptance from procurement for hard throttle vs. automatic charge-over.
- Concession we can offer: 20% off the surge premium for the first 500k burst tokens during the first 3 months if they sign a 12-month commit at +25% capacity.

I'll draft a follow-up email that addresses Jorge's line items and includes sample invoice math.

- Neha
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <acme-procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Dedicated Burst Add-on Structure & Cooldown SLAs

Jorge — thanks for the questions. Answers inline below, and I attached the short SOW (SOW-Acme-2026.docx) that aligns to the Pack B terms we discussed.

> Cooldown windows: can you confirm how the cooldown is measured? Is it per-GPU pool or per-route?

Good question — our recommended default is account-level cooldown per GPU pool to avoid noisy neighbors affecting other teams. That said, we can scope cooldowns by route at deployment time for teams that require isolation; that is part of Pack B (we'll configure isolate-by-route for critical routes).

> Billing treatment: does burst consumption draw down the reserved commit?

Two options (call out from Neha): by default bursts are separate add-on usage. Optionally for Pack B (higher commit) we can enable burst-to-commit conversion at a discounted internal transfer rate. If you want that we will include the logic in the SOW and billing terms.

> Surge cap: procurement prefers a $25k monthly cap and asks for throttle behavior.

We can support your $25k hard cap with two modes: (1) Soft mode: send alerts at thresholds and allow spend to continue until approval; (2) Hard mode: automatic throttling/failure of burst requests when cap is reached. We will default to soft mode unless procurement signs off on hard mode. We will include a toggle in Console + notify billing contacts on thresholds.

Attached: SOW-Acme-2026.docx (scope + acceptance), and an example invoice breakdown is embedded in RDW-burst-pricing-v3.pdf.

Next steps: If Acme is comfortable with the $25k cap with hard-throttle opt-in, we will:
- Update term sheet to reflect Pack B commit incentive (12-month +25% commit -> 20% surge premium discount for first 500k tokens)
- Add route-level cooldown options in SOW for critical routes
- Prepare DocuSign for signatures

Please confirm direction and I will route to legal/procurement for signature-ready docs.

Thanks,
Monica
From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@acme.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Acme Procurement <acme-procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Dedicated Burst Add-on Structure & Cooldown SLAs

Thanks, Monica — that addresses our main concerns. A couple final asks before we sign: 

1) Can you add a measured throughput SLO for Pack B during bursts (e.g., 95th percentile tokens/sec guarantee in-region, with credits if we fall below)? If we are committing more capacity and depending on bursts for critical user journeys, we need measurable guarantees.
2) Please include an automatic hard cap toggle in the Console (procurement will evaluate; we want the option to enable immediately if unexpected spend occurs).
3) We will accept the 12-month +25% commit incentive path, subject to legal sign-off. Procurement asks that the SOW include an example invoice line item and a monthly burst-spend report cadence.

Please route the final SOW/Term Sheet to acme-procurement@acme.com and to me. We will then circulate to legal and respond through DocuSign.

If you can get this into DocuSign by EOD Thursday, we will prioritize review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Jorge
